introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2023. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all the tasks (Task I, Task II and Task III) specified in the question paper.**

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The booklet reproduced here contains four versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two, Group Three and Group Four (booklets 23/0595/3/Grp 1 to Grp 4); a candidate sits only ONE group. Each version has three tasks: Task I (word processing), Task II (spreadsheet) and Task III (a short exercise on HTML, on a database or on a C or Pascal program). The working files named in the tasks (the picture UN.jpg, the pictures of the authors) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**GROUP ONE - TASK I (15 marks)**

Text to type (the title, three paragraphs, the three-item list and the author line):

> Social media verification: assessing sources and visual content
>
> Social media has changed journalism practice. Real-time audience engagement has given rise to crowdsourcing content, and even reporting tasks like verification can now be outsourced to the audience$^{166}$. While journalism remains in essence, a discipline of verification$^{167}$, methods of verifying content and sources require constant updating to reflect the impacts of fast-changing digital technologies, online behaviours, and newsgathering practices. For example, during the Arab Spring, the concept of 'open verification' - a process of public, collaborative, real-time verification - began to surface. But this process remains contentious because of the risks associated with misinformation going viral in the course of attempting to verify information step-by-step in a public forum (i.e. a reporter sharing unverified information with a view to crowdsourcing the verification process)$^{168}$.
>
> Today, eyewitness accounts and visual content are amongst the most important and compelling tools a journalist or news publisher can draw on to tell a high impact story. In a breaking news scenario, speed is a critical factor in verifying information from social media$^{169}$.
>
> Journalists must be able to navigate vast amounts of information to get to sources, information and images that matter. The rapid growth in the amount of visual content (photos, videos and GIFs) uploaded to social platforms, is driven by three main factors:
>
> - The proliferation of camera-enabled smart and feature phones around the world
> - Increased access to inexpensive (and in some places, free) mobile data
> - The rise of global social networks and social messaging platforms on which anyone can publish content and build an audience
>
> By Tom Trewinnard and Fergus Bell

The superscript numbers 166 to 169 follow the words "audience", "verification", "process)" and "media".

questions.enonce_markdown: Launch the word processor in your computer and type the text above. Save as Task 1. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Open the word processor (for example *Microsoft Word* or *LibreOffice Writer*) and a new blank document.

1. Type the title, the three paragraphs, the sentence that introduces the list, the three list lines and the author line **exactly as printed**: same words, same punctuation (the quotation marks around 'open verification', the brackets in "(i.e. a reporter ... process)", the hyphens), same order. Press *Enter* only at the end of a paragraph, never at the end of a line: the lines wrap by themselves.
2. Type the four reference numbers 166, 167, 168 and 169 right after the words "audience", "verification", "process)" and "media" (they are formatted as superscripts in question c).
3. Run the spelling checker and compare with the printed text line by line.
4. *File* > *Save As* > file name **Task 1** > *Save* (in the candidate folder given by the supervisor).

Marking idea (6 marks): all paragraphs typed (2); text accurate with few or no errors (2); title, list lines and author line present (1); file saved under the right name (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Format the text as follows: use bold and a 20 points sans serif font for the title. *[2 marks]*
Use full text justification, a 12 points Times New Roman or a similar serif font, and a line spacing of 1.5 for the paragraphs. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select the paragraphs (all the body text, not the title), then:

1. *Home* > **Justify** (or *Ctrl + J*): the text lines up on both the left and right margins (full justification).
2. Font box: **Times New Roman** (a serif font); size box: **12**.
3. *Home* > *Paragraph* (or *Line and Paragraph Spacing*) > **Line spacing: 1.5 lines**.

Marking idea (2 marks): full justification (1); serif font 12 pt (0.5); line spacing 1.5 (0.5).

questions.enonce_markdown: Format the four superscript numbers (166 - 169) as indicated in the text. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A superscript is a small character raised above the line. For each of the four numbers:

1. Select the number only (166 after "audience", 167 after "verification", 168 after "process)", 169 after "media").
2. Click the **Superscript** button ($x^2$) in the *Font* group, or press *Ctrl + Shift + =* (in LibreOffice Writer: *Ctrl + Shift + P*).
3. Check that the four numbers are now small and raised, like footnote references.

Marking idea (2 marks): 1 mark for two numbers correctly raised, 1 mark for all four.

questions.enonce_markdown: Use bullets to list out the last three lines as shown. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select the three lines that start with "The proliferation...", "Increased access..." and "The rise of global..." (the author line is not part of the list), then click the **Bullets** button in the *Paragraph* group (*Home* tab). Each line now starts with a round bullet and has the usual list indentation.

Marking idea (1 mark): the three lines (and only these three) bulleted.

questions.enonce_markdown: Insert the image UN.jpg before the title of the document. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The picture file UN.jpg is supplied on the day (in the candidate folder or on the desktop); it is not reproduced here.

1. Click at the very beginning of the document, before the title, and press *Enter* once so that there is an empty line above the title; move the cursor onto this empty line.
2. *Insert* > **Pictures** (in LibreOffice: *Insert* > *Image*) > select **UN.jpg** > *Insert*.
3. Resize the picture so that it is not too large (hold the *Shift* key while dragging a corner so that the shape is not distorted) and check that it appears **above** the title and that the title is still at the top of the text.

Marking idea (2 marks): picture inserted (1); placed before (above) the title (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Save your document as Task 2. *[no mark printed]*

*File* > *Print*: check the preview (the picture, the title, the justified paragraphs, the bullets and the four superscripts), choose the printer and the number of copies (1), then click *Print*.
